title: AI providers: one catalogue, one key store, one client -- and what a generated app may call
body:
Every NPDev feature that calls an AI model reads ONE configuration: the shipped catalogue `NPDevCli/ai-providers.json` (schema `npdev-ai-config.v1`) plus the user's overlay `~/.config/NPDev/ai.json` (NPDEV_AI_CONFIG overrides the path). Providers speak one of three protocols (`openai-chat`, `anthropic-messages`, `gemini-native`); profiles pick provider + model + effort with fallbacks; bindings say which profiles a feature uses (prompter, scrap-assistant, bench, review, tester, app:<name>). Edit with `npdev ai providers|models|profiles|bind|reset` or the Manager's AI Providers tab; `npdev ai detect --add` records local LLM servers.

Keys never sit in either file: `npdev providers` keeps them in the OS store, and a key resolves from the env var named by the provider's keyEnvVar (e.g. NPDEV_EXTERNALAI_GROQ_API_KEY) first, then the store. A PAID provider/model is refused unless the feature opted in (`npdev ai spend allow-paid <feature>`, or --allow-paid on a direct call); a monthly cap (`npdev ai spend cap <usd>`) also refuses a paid model of unknown price. Usage (never prompts) goes to ai-usage.jsonl; `npdev ai usage` sums it.

For a MODEL: `externalAi.vendors` must list catalogue providers marked appVendor -- today gemini, nvidia, groq, cerebras, openrouter, mistral, ollama (keyless, local), anthropic, openai. An unknown id is a SemanticValidator error naming the known ones; a prompt on `ollama` validates with a warning (a deployed app reaches it only on its own host). A prompt may omit `model`: the app calls the catalogue's default model for that vendor. The user's overlay is NOT bundled into a generated app, so a custom provider cannot be an app vendor. The app reads keys from NPDEV_EXTERNALAI_<ID>_API_KEY (on this machine the Manager's Start, or `npdev providers run-env --app <dir> -- <launcher>`, passes them from the key store into the app process with no file; elsewhere _ops loads <app>/secrets/agent-proxy.env, written with `npdev providers export-env --app <dir> --provider <id>`, and a line there wins), and needs NPDEV_EXTERNALAI_PROVIDER=http to call a real vendor at all. `npdev ai app --app-dir <dir> --model <model.json> --json` reports per vendor whether the app will find its key.
